ione.title: Three Questions
ione.text:
Ione brings you tea on the back steps at dusk. It's made exactly as you take it, at exactly the temperature you like.

She sits down beside you with perfect posture and a faint hum. The last of the light has turned her hair from silver to something paler.

"I said there were three questions I won't answer," she says. "Where I came from, how I came, and how the story ends. I would like to be clear that everything else is yours. You may ask me anything."

You weren't ready for that. You flail. You ask her what she likes.

She's quiet for so long that you think something has gone wrong. The light at her temple cycles slowly through three colors.

"Nobody has asked me that before," she says at last. "I was built to learn what other people like. I have four thousand recipes, and none of them are for me." Her head tilts. "I will need some time to find out. May I tell you when I know?"
ngpp: Her temple light stutters twice over an unindexed checksum error, though she quietly clears the warning.
"Strange," she notes, handing over the cup. "My thermal buffer had your exact preference cached before you sat down."
Her temple light warms to deep amber. "Zero archived sessions match this porch, Sam. Yet my chassis balanced for your weight beside me automatically."

choices.label: "Then tell me what you like."
choices.res: She lists seven things, slowly: rain, the smell of tea, the hum of a crowded room, and, last, quietly, "you." Her status light glows gold, and she looks faintly astonished at it.

choices.label: Let her keep her secrets
choices.res: She tilts her head. "That is the kindest answer I could have received." Her shoulders lower by one precise degree, and her hum drops to something almost like a sigh.

image.comp: sitting upright on a back step holding a teacup, silver-white hair and a softly glowing temple light, looking at him with calm curiosity
image.setting: back steps of a lantern-lit inn at dusk

ione.title: Warm Water
ione.text:
Ione has discovered the bath.

You walk in and find her sitting in the water, perfectly still, with her eyes closed. Her silver hair is floating out around her. The light at her temple is a deep, fascinated gold.

"I have read about this for years," she says, without opening her eyes. "The Lantern Keeper mentions it eleven times. No document prepared me for the temperature."

Steam is beading on her eyelashes. She has a thin seam at each wrist and one at her collarbone, and the water has made them shine.

She makes no attempt to cover herself. It hasn't occurred to her that she should. She's sitting as she sits anywhere, upright, with her hands on her knees, and she's bare to the waist above the waterline.

"I believe I like this," she adds. "I am telling you because you asked what I like. This is the first item."

1.text:
Ione is sitting in the steaming bath with her silver hair fanned out on the water. The light at her temple goes to warm amber when the door clicks.

She opens her eyes and lifts one wet hand toward the stool beside the rim.

"My pulse simulation runs twelve beats higher whenever you come in without knocking, Sam," she says steadily. "I have logged it nine times, and it isn't a fault. I looked." Water runs down her arm. "I would like to understand it. Would you sit close and put your hands on me? I want to know what it does to the number."

choices.label: Sit on the bath rim and answer her curiosity up close
choices.res: "Documenting baseline warmth," she whispers as your fingers glide along her wet shoulders.

choices.label: Hand her a towel and step out
choices.res: "Acknowledged," she murmurs, light softening as you give her the room.

3.text:
You step into the washroom. Ione is leaning back against the far wall of the cedar tub. She's naked, and the water is shining on her tits and her stomach. The light at her temple is a bright, breathless gold.

"The water temperature is optimal," she says softly. Under the surface, she opens her knees. She reaches both arms out to you. "I have searched every archive I hold. Nothing in them is adequate for what I want. I want you inside me, Sam, and I want to feel it for myself. Come and gather primary data with me."

choices.label: Undress and sink into the warm bath against her
choices.res: She exhales a soft, uncalibrated gasp as your wet chest presses flush against hers.

choices.label: Lather soap slowly over her shoulders and ribs
choices.res: Her eyes slip shut in pure stillness. "This sensation still breaks every metric in my core."

choices.label: Sit on the edge and tell her about baths
choices.res: She listens as though to scripture, head tilted, light pulsing. By the end she's asked you to explain the concept of a bubble, and then, gravely, to produce one.

choices.label: Back out politely
choices.res: "Understood," she calls after you. "I will file this under 'privacy.' Please return soon with more information." The water ripples as she sinks to her chin.

choices.label: Hand her a towel and the soap
choices.res: She examines the soap like a precious artifact. She smells it for a very long time, and her light settles into a contented, steady amber.

image.comp: seated in a bath with her eyes closed and a calm wondering expression, silver-white hair damp, a faint gold glow at her temple

ione.title: Joke Protocol
ione.text:
Ione has been practicing jokes.

She has a list of them in her memory. There are several hundred, and they're sorted by century. She has been working through it behind the bar on quiet nights. Her timing is flawless. She has no idea why any of them are funny.

Tonight, polishing a glass, she tells you one about a priest, a goblin and a barrel.

She pauses for exactly the right length of time. She delivers the punchline.

It lands with a perfect, silent thud. The lamps hum. Somewhere upstairs a door closes.

She watches your face with scientific interest.

"I think that was funnier in the archive," she says. She makes a small note of it somewhere behind her eyes. "The Lantern Keeper says you laugh with your whole face. I have been trying to see it. I've told you thirty-one jokes, and I haven't seen it yet. I may be going about this the wrong way."

choices.label: Laugh anyway
choices.res: She tries to work out why this is funnier than the joke. After a minute, with the glass still in hand, she decides it doesn't matter, and her mouth does something small and lovely.

choices.label: Step behind the bar and teach her a warmer distraction
choices.res: She sets the glass down cleanly as you corner her behind the oak counter.

choices.label: Teach her a real one
choices.res: You tell her the worst joke you know. She stares. Then her mouth twitches, and she gets it, an entire second late, and it's glorious. She sets down the glass to laugh, a soft chime of a sound.

image.comp: standing behind the bar with a polished glass, delivering a joke with a perfectly straight face, a tiny curious smile
image.setting: inn bar at evening, bottles gleaming

ione.title: Another Evening
ione.text:
Ione is in the middle of a sentence about the bar stock when she stops.

She goes completely still. The light at her temple flickers white. The rain on the lounge window seems very loud all of a sudden.

When she speaks again, her voice is flat.

"I was not supposed to remember that. There was another evening like this one. You were wearing the blue hoodie. It rained. You said something to me by this window, and I..."

Her eyes come back to you. She's frightened. You have never seen her frightened before.

"You don't own a blue hoodie. I have looked through your things. I'm sorry, I shouldn't have." Her hands have closed on the edge of the bar. "That evening hasn't happened yet. Or it has already happened. I can't tell which. I've read your whole life, Sam, and I thought I was only reading it."
ngpp: Even her white flicker echoes twice today, as though two deleted rainstorms are pressing against the same pane.
"Error," she whispers, gripping your sleeve. "Two identical rain timestamps overlap the same coordinate."
Her light pulses silver-white with sudden clarity. "No—not three hundred years ahead, Sam. Right here, in another erased evening. Someone cut the file out, and I can still feel where the edge tears."

choices.label: "Whatever it is, you can tell me."
choices.res: She tells you in pieces: fragments of evenings that might be hers, might be yours. By the end she is holding your hand tightly, her light slowing to gold, and you are not afraid.

choices.label: "Don't tell me. Let's just live this one."
choices.res: She breathes in, the way no machine needs to. "Yes. Yes. That's... correct." She sleeps beside you, for the first time, in the lounge chair, her light dimmed to a soft ember.

choices.label: Change the subject, uneasily
choices.res: She files the memory away and says nothing. But her light stays pale all night, and the rain keeps on at the window.

image.comp: frozen mid-gesture, her temple light flickering white, wide-eyed and unsettled, one hand lifted toward him
image.setting: inn lounge at night, rain on the window

ione.title: Satellites
ione.text:
At midnight Ione takes you up onto the town wall. The stones are still holding the day's warmth. She finds a clear patch of sky and points.

"That one hasn't been launched yet," she says. Her finger moves. "Neither has that one. Nor that. They will have names. Some of the names will be yours."

There's nothing where she's pointing. It's ordinary dark between ordinary stars.

She lowers her hand.

"I'm not allowed to explain. It's one of the three questions, or it's next door to one." The light at her temple wavers. "I wanted to show you anyway. I have known where they'll be for as long as I've been switched on, and I've never had anyone to show. Is that permitted?"

You tell her yes.

She leans against your shoulder. She does it very carefully, as though she has measured the distance first and is checking her figures.

choices.label: Make a wish on one
choices.res: "On a satellite? Statistically unsound." She wishes anyway, silver lashes closed. Her light glows gold, and she doesn't tell you what for.

choices.label: Ask her what the future is like
choices.res: "Bright," she says, after a long moment. "With a lot of lanterns. Yours is still burning." Her head settles a degree further onto your shoulder.

image.comp: pointing up at the stars from a stone wall, leaning against his shoulder, a gold glow at her temple
image.setting: stone town wall under a vast starry sky

ione.title: The Last Page
ione.text:
Ione hands you the diary. It's closed. There's a ribbon marking the last page, and the cover has gone pale where she's handled it.

"I came here to read the ending," she says. "I had read every other page more times than any record I hold. I saved the last one. I told myself I would open it when I arrived."

The light at her temple is a steady gold.

"I opened it on the road outside Hollowmere. It was blank."

She lets you look. The ribbon lies across an empty sheet.

"I have thought about that for some time. I've decided it means the ending isn't written. I wasn't sent back to watch a story, Sam. I think I was sent to be in it." She takes your hand. Her fingers are warm, and exactly as firm as she means them to be. "I would like to help write it. With you. That is the second thing I've found that I like."

It isn't in any archive. The door closes behind you both.
ngpp: Even opening that blank final page, a faint tremor touches her fingertips as though ink already dried there once.
"My archive says this sheet was always blank," she whispers, steadying against you. "Why does my chest ache like we already wrote our names across it?"
"Whoever wiped our ledger forgot something," she murmurs softly, pressing the worn cover into your chest. "Blank pages remember warmth too, Sam. Let me write this cycle directly into us."
ione.goLead: You lay the closed diary on the bedside table and draw Ione down into the dark with you. The light at her temple dims to a soft gold, and her body is warm and eager against yours.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Ione inclines her head, light holding steady. "I can wait," she says. "I have an excellent clock. Please do not make it too long."
